Senses.Explanation: The buddha-way does not appear before him, nor does he attain buddhahood — the Lotus line of the ten-eon seat, ten eons of sitting with nothing shown and nothing attained, which the Chan halls pried open for six centuries: granting more eons, turning the question back, ruling the neat answers dead, and finding the buddha in the night voice itself. Ying'an Tanhua, in the hall at the Jianfu temple: the Great-Unhindered-Wisdom-Victorious buddha sat ten eons in the seat of the way, and the buddha-way did not appear before him, nor did he attain buddhahood. At the patch-robed gate this comes a little nearer. And the one line kneaded with mud and water — how is it said? Once authority is in hand, watch the command go forth. Gulin Qingmao, at the opening of the hall on Mount Tianping, is asked it straight: ten eons seated in the seat of the way, the buddha-way not appearing, no buddhahood attained — at such a time, what? His answer: give him ten more eons to begin with. The monk presses on — where there is spirit, add spirit; where there is no flair, flair as well — and he closes: beware of seeking it from him; far off, it estranges itself from you. Changmu Guangdian, at the Mituo temple, turns the line on itself: seated in the seat of the way — why no attaining of buddhahood? Having attained buddhahood — why does the buddha-way not appear? The Great-Wisdom-Victorious is a spirit-turtle dragging its tail, toil that only sweeps its own tracks. He raises Guizong — how is one a buddha? You yourself are; keep to it — one film in the eye and empty blossoms fall in profusion — then resolves: whole mind is buddha, whole buddha is mind, mind and buddha not two, that one and this one without difference. Free of mind-face and buddha-face — that is truly seated in the seat of the way; free of I and I-view — that is truly attaining buddhahood. Already buddha — why then does the buddha-way not appear? Only because one cannot turn mountains, rivers, and the great earth back into oneself, cannot turn oneself back into mountains, rivers, and the great earth. Therefore the buddha-way does not appear, nor is buddhahood attained. He calls Xuedou's Thousand peaks, cold color the one turning, and Rain dripping on rock flowers the other, lifts the staff — this is a staff: what do you call mountains, rivers, and the great earth? — and after the silence: quite a leak all the same. Shengke Deyu, in the exchange records: the layman Yishui raises the old asking — the monk had asked, and Yune answered: ravines are easy to fill, the human heart hard to satisfy — and asks his ruling on it. Shengke: that is a plainly apt dead phrase. Pressed — ten eons seated in the seat of the way, why no buddhahood? — he answers: it has doubted men to death, ancient and modern. And he seals it with a verse: the fine face shows a little — why still shield it with the sleeve? Doubting men to death past counting; half-longing, half-rueful to the sky's edge. Pufu Zhuo, preaching at the precept platform of the Yuantong hermitage: the buddha sat ten eons in the seat of the way, the buddha-way did not appear before him, nor did he attain buddhahood. Good people — take this very precept platform, night after night the buddha-voice resounding: what do you know the buddha to be? Buddha means awake; awake means waking. And waking — what is woken? Through the twelve hours of the day, in speech, silence, laughter, ease — what do you know this to be? Turning the head in the cold, all by the buddha's strength, treating enemy and kin level — only then are you allowed the name of a gone-from-home patch-robed monk. Do you not know the saying: night after night I sleep with the buddha in my arms; morning after morning we rise together; sitting, standing, ever at his side; speech and silence dwell together; not a hair's shift, like form and shadow. To know where the buddha goes — only this sound of the voice is it.
